sources.quote: Few of the roughly 70 Republican-appointed judges eligible to take a form of partial retirement or completely step down from the bench as of June 1 have done so, denying Trump the chance to pick their replacement.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest same-finding coverage found: GOP-appointed eligible judges not stepping back under Trump 2. Headline 'Conservative Judges Shun Retirement Under Trump Second Term'; dek says over 100 GOP-appointed judges eligible to retire but haven't. No 16-of-83 count.

sources.quote: Forty-six Republican appointees are now eligible (22 appellate, 24 district), but 37 of them have been eligible since Biden was inaugurated.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff. Says most currently eligible GOP appointees are long-time stayers, and that Trump 2 has the lowest vacancy creation of the last five administrations over ~20 months from Election Day (42 vs 97 in Trump 1). Different eligible-pool count (46 now eligible, not 83) and different window.

sources.quote: Almost all of the judges eligible for senior status now were also eligible in 2020, long before Emil Bove.
sources.searcher_note: Circuit judges only. Makes the lead's 'already passed under Trump 1' point in words: lists 20 GOP circuit judges eligible by Nov 2020. Also quotes Mike Fragoso (National Review) saying the same. Skeptical of the 'judges refusing because of Trump/Bove' narrative.

sources.quote: Only three of the almost two dozen Republican-appointed appeals judges eligible for partial retirement did so this year, the third doing so in October.
sources.searcher_note: Appeals judges only, calendar 2025: 3 of ~24 eligible GOP appointees took senior status.

sources.quote: it's notable that most of the more than 20 other retirement-eligible Republican-appointed appeals court judges—including two appointed by Trump in his first term, Ralph Erickson and Kurt Engelhardt—have so far decided to stay put.
sources.searcher_note: Progressive legal-commentary outlet. Also: since Trump's re-election only 34 judges created vacancies, 27 of them Republican appointees.

sources.quote: In Mr. Trump's first term, 15 Republican appointees to the appeals courts and four Democratic appointees left their seats within that same time frame.
sources.searcher_note: Compares Trump 1 vs Trump 2 appeals vacancies (15 GOP appointees then vs 3 in Trump 2 through his first year back). Appeals only.

notes: Several outlets report the same finding in words: GOP-appointed eligible judges mostly not taking senior status under Trump 2 (Bloomberg Law June 2025 earliest). Brookings (Wheeler, Aug 2026, post-cutoff) and Blackman/Fragoso make the lead's leftover-stayer point (most eligible GOP appointees have been eligible since 2020/2021). No source found with the lead's 16-of-83 (19.3%) count, the 517-day window, the 50-of-83 already-passed-under-Trump-1 figure, or the 20% Trump 1 comparison. Pool sizes in the press differ (roughly 70 as of June 2025; 46 now eligible per Brookings Aug 2026; ~22-24 appeals judges) because windows and eligibility definitions differ. No source found saying Trump 2 senior-status rates are ordinary or higher. Bloomberg Law 2026-05-26 'Timeline Narrows for Trump to Fill Judge Seats Before Midterms' and EPPC (Fragoso, 2026-03-04) were opened but had no counts; not recorded. National Review 'Senior-Eligible Judges' page returned no body text.
